about: Every number on these slides and in their speaker notes, with its source. The measured results come from synthetic tasks and published evidence; the two worked examples are illustrations, not measured runs.

claims.number: 0 tokens when the same pipeline is asked for again
claims.source: An illustration of how the work is organized, not a measured run: when search and retrieval return a stored solution, no model is called and no work is repeated. The zero-token result that is measured is narrower: compiled code recipes run as plain code, on the evidence slide.

claims.number: Hundreds of new memory systems for agents on GitHub within days
claims.source: The premise of this illustration, not a count we have recorded. No feed counts new memory systems yet.

claims.number: Feeds for new repos and papers, run by server workers
claims.source: Planned, not running. Tessera already serves the feed tools, and today the only feed that runs is the daily check of our own live services. Feeds for new repos, papers and model releases come next, starting from the tool-discovery and freshness-checks packs; the always-on server workers deck has the dated status.

claims.number: 705 of 739 public repos in the event directory scanned into nouns and verbs
claims.source: The real precedent for this illustration, and the same scan as the proof slide: a deterministic scan (hackscan 1.2.0) cloned each repo shallowly and read its tree without running any code, on October 29, 2026; 34 failed (24 empty, 5 not found or private, 5 timed out). Aggregate counts only.

claims.number: 59 seed packs in one library, with 1,177 nouns, 381 verb templates and 37 worked examples
claims.source: A count of the packs in the seed-pack library's README at commit d837b30, on October 30, 2026. They are proposals and validated examples: none is installed, imported, admitted or activated.
A continuous tuning loop built from nouns and verbs on one local GPU, October 29, 2026, scored on a frozen, synthetic tool-call test of 150 rows.
The same loop and the same frozen, synthetic test, October 29, 2026.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B: exact match 93.3% to 99.3%, +6.0 points, 95% CI +2.0 to +10.7; promotion rule 12 of 12
claims.source: QLoRA on free cloud GPUs for the same kind of synthetic task, scored on a fresh 150-row test whose hashes were registered before scoring. A fresh reload reproduced its outputs. The rule said promote; nothing has been promoted or admitted. The run record, with every file's hash, is published with this deck's evidence.

claims.number: 10/10 agent processes finished their shared tasks in one wave
claims.source: Ten native Pi processes on synthetic tasks, October 29, 2026. Earlier waves of 7/10 and 3/3 are also on record.

claims.number: 100/100 protocol clients in 25.7 seconds, with no rate-limit rejections
claims.source: A short protocol load test on October 29, 2026: 25.663 seconds and no HTTP 429. Expected write conflicts did occur. Not 100 separate agent programs.

claims.number: 6 agent programs each finished a scoped task; 6 of 14 attempts passed
claims.source: OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Muse Code, nanoMuse and OpenClaw in narrow lifecycle tests, with every failure recorded. A seventh program, Claude Code, passed a separate test later.

claims.number: 0 model tokens while compiled code recipes run
claims.source: Compiled recipes run as plain code; six local deterministic runs are recorded. Making or checking a recipe can still use a model.

claims.number: 16 of 16 receipts recompute for the film's production run
claims.source: The film's production ran as 16 claimed tasks of 7 verbs on a local Tessera store, with no model calls. The published bundle's verify.py recomputes every receipt with Tessera's rule, checks that 142 of 161 input pins are outputs of earlier receipted tasks (the rest are setup nouns), and ties all 12 published files to receipts. The store itself is not public.

claims.number: 705 of 739 public repos in the event directory scanned into nouns and verbs
claims.source: A deterministic scan (hackscan 1.2.0) cloned each repo shallowly and read its tree without running any code, on October 29, 2026; 34 failed (24 empty, 5 not found or private, 5 timed out). Aggregate counts only.

claims.number: 58.9% of scanned repos reference Meta's model API; 4.3% use MCP
claims.source: 415 of 705 scanned repos contain the text api.meta.ai, and 30 show an MCP signal (an SDK dependency, server code, tool definitions or client config). Mentions are text matches, not proof of use.
